The test image shows a corn ear viewed from the tip/butt end. Key observations:
- White cottony/fluffy mycelial growth at the center of the cob
- Kernels discolored to grayish-white/olive tones
- Some dark black spotting on kernels
- Pinkish-reddish discoloration between kernel rows
- Husks are dry and tan-colored

This is an ear rot. Candidates: Diplodia (white cottony mycelium), Fusarium (white-to-pink), or Gibberella (pink-red). Let me view reference images.
The Diplodia reference shows uniform white cottony coating on chalky kernels. Fusarium shows white-to-pink patchy mycelium on yellow kernels. Let me view more reference images to narrow down further.

Now I can clearly rule out:
- **Aspergillus**: olive-green powdery mold — not present
- **Trichoderma**: blue-green mold — not present  
- **Common_smut**: large pale galls — not present

**Analysis of test image features:**
- Cross-section (tip-end view) of a corn ear
- Dense white cottony mycelium at the cob center, filling between kernels
- Kernels are grayish-white, chalky, and shrunken-looking
- Some dark spots/specks on kernels (possible pycnidia)
- Some pinkish-reddish tissue between kernels

**Comparing to candidates:**
- **Diplodia**: white-to-grayish-white cottony mycelium, chalky/tan shrunken kernels, tiny black pycnidia — matches very well (grayish-white kernels, white mycelium, dark specks)
- **Fusarium**: white-to-pinkish discrete tufts on otherwise yellow/normal kernels — less consistent; test image kernels are uniformly discolored, not yellow
- **Gibberella**: pink-to-reddish-purple mold at silk/tip end — test image doesn't show the diagnostic reddish-purple coloration on kernels

The uniformly chalky/grayish-white kernels, the dense white cottony mycelium filling the cob center, and potential black pycnidia specks all point strongly to **Ear_rots_Diplodia**.

The uniform chalky kernel discoloration and white mycelium pattern matches Diplodia ear rot; not Fusarium (which shows discrete tufts on yellow kernels) or Gibberella (which shows diagnostic pink-red mold)."}
